List.title: KIN CP2001827 27CSP001 North Tower Rm Renovations

Detail.title: KIN CP2001827 27CSP001 North Tower Rm Renovations
Detail.description: This project includes 10 non-ADA Jack and Jill suites, 3 single rooms with attached bathroom, 2 accessible Jack and Jill suites with roll-in showers, 1 accessible Jack and Jill suite with a transfer shower, 1 single accessible room with attached bathroom with a roll-in shower, and 1 single accessible room with attached bathroom with a transfer shower on Level 1 at the North Tower. This project consists of the following: Demolition of flooring, walls, plumbing fixtures, wall and floor tile, doors, built-in furniture, and ceilings of  9 rooms and 5 bathrooms on Level 1 as well as doors at Rooms 158 and 160, where walls within suite were previously demolished to become fully ADA/TAS compliant accessible rooms and suites as described above. New work to include new walls, doors, plumbing re-build to tie into new chase walls, plumbing fixtures, and toilet accessories at new accessible suites as described above. All 32 rooms in scope to receive new flooring, base, paint, HVAC pony wall surround, sink and faucet in cabinet, tackboards, paint, and drywall where indicated. Power is existing and will be connected to new devices within 6’ of original location. New Lounge at North Tower Entry will be incorporated, capturing demolished resident room 152 to provide an accessible route from ground level to Level 1 resident rooms with the incorporation of a pit-free, ramp-free, electric chair lift.  A small slab addition will be incorporated to infill a small area adjacent to the new chair lift location for acontinuous floor at the new Lounge 152.

Detail.title: Grazing Lease at Palo Duro Canyon State Park for the Upper Mesquite Mesa (1,523 acres), Lower Mesquite Mesa (523 acres) and Cita Canyon (1,419 acres) Pastures
Detail.nigpCodes: 97135-Land, Rental Or Lease;
Detail.description:
Notice is hereby given that Texas Parks and WildlifeDepartment (TPWD) is accepting bids for a livestock-grazing lease at the PaloDuro Canyon State Park, located in Randall and Armstrong Counties, Texas.

Acreage to be included in the lease will be approximately threethousand four hundred sixty-five (3,465) acres. Pasture areas include the UpperMesquite Mesa (1,523 acres), Lower Mesquite Mesa (523 acres) and Cita Canyon (1,419acres).

ATTENTION:Due to the topography of the area, the grazing lease area is landlockedproperty that does not touch a public roadway and has no vehicular accessexcept by crossing the Lighthouse Ranch, a private property. Therefore, thissolicitation is being advertised under Texas Government Code, Section 2155.067.TPWD believes that the service is proprietary to one vendor and/or to thespecification.  Only responses conforming exactly to these specificationswill be considered in determining an award. TPWD strongly encourages responsesfrom all qualified vendors who may be able to provide the specified service.

List.title: Special Education Contracted Services

Detail.title: Special Education Contracted Services
Detail.description:
PURPOSE
In order to be in compliance with federal, state and local purchasing laws, the Birdville Independent School District (BISD) is soliciting competitive sealed proposals for Special Education Contracted Services.
 
This contract is intended to be a multi-award contract for services provided on an as-needed basis by personnel who are not on the payroll of the district. Services delivered are by either an independent contractor or a contracting firm that offers these services to the public. Such services are paid on a fee basis for specialized services that are usually considered to be temporary or short term in nature, normally in an area that supplements the expertise in the school district.
 
Based on the 2025-2026 expenditures and the Consumer Price Index published in September 2026, the cost-price analysis for this contract is $398,494.30.
 
CONTRACT TERM AND RENEWALS
This proposal shall be effective from December 1, 2026 through November 30, 2027. The District and Proposer may, upon mutual consent, extend the contract for three (3) additional one-year periods (not to exceed a total of 4 years) upon written request of the Proposer presented no later than forty-five (45) days prior to the expiration of the contract.
 
The rates can be adjusted upward or downward based on the price change specifications each six (6) months if agreeable to the district. If agreement cannot be reached, the contract is terminated at the end of the current contract period.

An additional ninety (90) day transitional period shall be added to the end of the contractual agreement if desired by the district. The contractual prices, terms and conditions shall remain in force during the transitional period.
 
PROPOSAL SUBMISSION
Late proposals will not be accepted. No verbal, telephonic, electronic mail or faxed responses will be considered. The preferred method of delivery is through the e-bid system; however, paper responses will be accepted in the Purchasing Department prior to the due date and time. To receive a paper version, please contact Purchasing via phone 817-547-5629 or by email bisd.purchasing@birdvilleschools.net.

List.title: P#1112666 | Centennial Program | New Park Development | Silver Lake State Park

Detail.title: P#1112666 | Centennial Program | New Park Development | Silver Lake State Park
Detail.description:
The Infrastructure Division of the Texas Parksand Wildlife Department (TPWD) is issuing a Request for Proposals (RFP) fora Construction Manager-at-Risk (CMR). This solicitation will follow a one-stepRFP process in accordance with Texas Government Code Section 2269.253.

 

Project Number: 1112666

Project Name: Centennial Program – New Park Development

Project Location: Silver Lake State Park; Edwards andKinney Counties, Texas

Solicitation: Construction Manager at Risk

Construction Cost Estimate: $35 Million

 

ConstructionManager-at-Risk Deliverables:

 

PARTONE - PRE-CONSTRUCTION: The awarded Contractor shall collaborate with TPWD and itsArchitects and Engineers during the development of construction documents,including review and comment exercises on Schematic Design; Design Development;and 50%, 95% and 100% Construction Documents. The Contractor’s expertise will be used to guide value engineering,constructability decisions, construction phasing, and ultimately set theGuaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) within the limits established by the contract.The services during Pre-Construction shall include but not be limited to; attendingmeetings, plan reviews, constructability reviews and cost estimating.  The Contractor shall be proactive inrecommending strategies to help minimize impact to the schedule and budget.Certain activities that serve to maintain the project schedule and budget maybe conducted during Pre-Construction Services; such as permitting coordination,early procurement planning for long lead items, Design- Assistance (ifneeded) and early engagement of major subcontractors.

 

PARTTWO – CONSTRUCTION: Inaccordance with the approved schedule and GMP, the Contractor shall facilitatebidding and selection of labor in accordance with state requirements for goodfaith effort to engage Veteran Heroes United in Businesses, and provide for allmaterials, installations, labor, coordination, management and supervisoryactivities necessary to complete construction of the project in accordance withthe drawings, specifications and other contract documents that will be preparedby the Architect, Engineers and TPWD.

 

General Scope of Work

 

Project No. 1112666 titled “Centennial Program– New Park Development” is being solicited to develop a newly acquired over50,000 acre ranch tract in Edwards and Kinney Counties for a new Silver LakeState Park for the state of Texas. The acquired property is located approximately 25 miles south of RockSprings, Texas and 11 miles west of Camp Wood, Texas and includes riverfrontage.  The tract’s geographiclocation is approximately Latitude 29°33’ N; Longitude 100°12’ W. 

 

The scope of this project includespre-construction services and construction of the new park development.  The following list outlines the desired scopecomponents for the new park development. Under the Construction Manager at Risk(CMR) delivery method, the selected CMR will collaborate with TPWD and theArchitect/Engineer of Record to evaluate feasibility, prioritize scope, andalign work with available funding as the project progresses to deliver thehighest achievable value within the established budget and performance period.

 

TPWD plans for the fully constructed park toinclude but not be limited to:

 

  • Park entry and monument signage

 

  • Electrical access gate(s)

 

  • Paved Roadways including low water crossing(s)

 

  • Gravel Roadways

 

  • Parkwide directional signage

 

  • Operational Facilities to include Park Headquarters, staff residences, park host sites, maintenance yard and supporting buildings

 

  • Day Use Facilities to include trailheads, multi-use trails, picnic areas, group pavilion(s), amphitheater, Nature Center, playground, wildlife viewing areas, restrooms, parking areas

 

  • Overnight Facilities to include developed and primitive camping areas, mini-cabins, screened shelters, restrooms and associated parking areas

 

  • Site utilities including a public water system, wastewater treatment facilities, electrical infrastructure, telecommunications infrastructure, radio tower and associated infrastructure

 

  • Sustainable systems

 

  • Site demolition

 

  • Historic structures renovation / reuse

 

 

Solicitation Documents

 

TPWD uses an online e‑bid system calledCobbleStone, known as the “Vendor Gateway,” for all solicitations. Proposersmust sign in or create a Vendor Gateway account to participate in thesubmission process. All proposals must be submitted electronically through theVendor Gateway on or before the Submission Deadline stated in the solicitationdocuments, which are available on the Vendor Gateway. Submissions sent by mail,telephone, fax, email, or any method other than the Vendor Gateway will not beaccepted, considered, or acknowledged.

 

VendorGateway Sign In/Create Account: https://tpwd.cobblestone.software/Gateway/Default.aspx

 

Solicitationdocuments are available through the Vendor Gateway at the link provided below:

 

https://tpwd.cobblestone.software/Gateway/solicitationdetails?solicid=67

Detail.title: Request for Proposals for Transmission to Information Returns Intake System (IRIS) Services
Detail.description:
EMPLOYEES RETIREMENT SYSTEM OF TEXAS

REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS FOR

TRANSMISSION TO INFORMATION RETURNS INTAKE SYSTEM (IRIS) SERVICES

 SOLICITATION NO. 26-15697-001

NIGP CODE:  208-00, 208-11, 208-36, 208-80, 920-17

The Employees Retirement System of Texas (ERS) has issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) seeking a qualified firm (Respondent) to provide an enterprise-grade tax compliance software to implement a transmission to Information Return Intake System (IRIS) for validating, processing, and electronically filing IRS Form 1099-R (Distributions from Pensions, Annuities, Retirement or Profit-Sharing Plans, IRAs, Insurance Contracts, etc.). Respondent shall provide the level of services required in the RFP and meet other requirements that are in the best interests of ERS, its members, and the state of Texas (State).


Respondent shall be required to execute a contract (Contract) satisfactory to, ERS for a period that begins upon execution of the Contract by ERS and extends for four (4) years, with an option to extend upon agreement of both parties. It is anticipated the Contract will be executed in October 2026.


To be eligible for consideration, Respondent is required to submit its response to the RFP (Proposal) in accordance with the instructions set forth in the RFP. Respondents must meet the Minimum Requirements set forth in Section B of the Respondent Questionnaire (Appendix E). All Proposal materials shall be received by ERS via Euna Procurement no later than October 20, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. CT.


The RFP is posted to the ESBD. To submit a Proposal, prospective Respondents must first create a profile in Euna Procurement (ERS’ e-procurement portal located at erstexas.bonfirehub.com),which operates best on the latest versions of Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome, and Mozilla Firefox. Browser cookies must be enabled when accessing Euna Procurement. Note that Respondent’s primary Proposal contact must create a Euna Procurement profile (with the actual contact person’s email address) and download the RFP documents in order to send and receive messages via Euna Procurement.


ERS reserves the right to rebid the RFP if deemed by ERS to be in the best interests of ERS, its members, and/or the State. ERS also reserves the right to reject any Proposal submitted that does not fully comply with the RFP’s instructions and criteria. ERS is under no legal requirement to execute a Contract on the basis of this notice or upon issuance of the RFP and will not pay any costs incurred by any Respondent in connection with the preparation of a Proposal. ERS also reserves the right to revise any provisions set forth in the RFP at any time prior to execution of a Contract where ERS deems it to bein the best interests of ERS, its members, and/or the State.


Any general questions should be sent to ERS’ point of contact, Office of Procurement and Contract Oversight, via Euna Procurement or ivendorquestions@ers.texas.gov. ERS’ mailing address is P.O. Box 13207, Austin, Texas 78711-3207.

List.title: Emergency Ground Support Equipment Rental

Detail.title: Emergency Ground Support Equipment Rental
Detail.description: The Statewide Procurement Division (SPD), a division of CPA, requests sealed responses for Emergency Ground Support Equipment Rental The major customer for these items and services is the Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM). These services and commodities are required for all-hazards emergency preparedness and response and may be simultaneously dispatched to one or more locations throughout the state of Texas prior to, during, or after an incident or event occurs. All-hazards planning and preparedness addresses natural, technological, adversarial, or human caused incidents or events. CPA and TDEM particularly seek to prepare for events like the recent natural disaster Hurricane Harvey, which in 2017 inflicted $125 billion in damages and displaced over 30,000 people. Historically, the services requested under this RFP are used by the Customer for periods ranging from 4 days to 6 weeks, but the duration is dependent upon the scale and scope of the emergency. Therefore, rental periods may be required for both short and long durations, as needed.

This mandatory Space-Fit/Configuration Layout must be submitted electronically by email to FY27CampMabryPortables@cfmo.mil.texas.gov

Detail.title: FORMAL REQUEST FOR OFFER FOR FIRE STATION No. 3 MINI SPLIT
Detail.nigpCodes: 91017-Energy Computerized Control System (Hvac, Lighting, Utilities, Etc) Installation, Maintenance And Repair Services;
Detail.description: The City of San Antonio is soliciting an offer to removethe existing equipment and provide and install two new Daikin 4-ton Mini Splitsystems to handle the load of the Fire Station No. 3 building. Work willinclude installing two new condensers with a capacity of 48,000 BTU, run newcopper lines to the indoor air handlers that will be installed in the roomswhere no Mini Split exists at this time. The line sets on the exterior wall isto be run inside a line hide cover, run all electrical circuits to all theindoor air handler as well as the condensers, run all the condensate lines toan indoor drain, perform the start-up and to ensure the systems are fullyfunctional. Work will also include removing the shop heater on the second floorand safely cap off the gas line. Work must be done in a manner to minimize any structural work. If any structural work is needed, such as cutting holes in theceilings or walls, vendor will perform the modifications and attempt toreattach the cut pieces back to their original place as best as possible.

Detail.description:
Introduction

The issuing office believes that the requested Services in this Request for Proposals maybe proprietary to one vendor under Section 2155.067 of the Government Code; however, the issuing office strongly encourages offers from all qualified Respondents that may be able to provide the requested items.

The Health and Human Services Commission (“Owner”), for and on behalf of its Health and Specialty Care System Division (“HSCS”), is soliciting Competitive Sealed Proposals (“Proposals”) for selection of a General Contractor (“Contractor”) to provide general construction and construction administration services to the Owner for Project No.24-119-LBL, Fire Alarm Panel Upgrade at Lubbock State Supported Living Center (the “Project”), in accordance with the terms, conditions, and requirements set forth in this Solicitation.

Project Location, Summary, and Budget  

Project Location:

Lubbock State Supported Living Center

3401 N University Ave,

Lubbock, TX, 79415

Project Summary: The Scope of Work includes, but is not limited to, the following:

The Fire Alarm System Installing Contractor shall furnish all labor, equipment, and materials, and perform all operations in connection with the demolition of the existing fire alarm system and the installation of a new, addressable fire alarm system throughout the designated buildings on the Lubbock State Supported Living Center in Lubbock, Texas, as indicated and described in the contract drawings and specifications. Other than where noted by the design documents, the existing fire alarm system shall remain fully operational until acceptance of the new fire alarm system. Only compatible systems conforming exactly to the designated specifications, which include proposing only the brand name(s), make and model number(s) specified,will be considered.

For complete Project information, refer to Attachment(s) H to Exhibit C, Project Specifications and Drawings (if there are separate drawings for the Project). 

Project Estimate: The approximate cost for construction of the Project is $3,676,427.00

 Optional Pre-Proposal Webinar

 HHSC will conduct one (1) optional pre-proposal webinar that will be held on the date and

time described below. Attendance at the pre-proposal webinar is optional.

Pre-Proposal Webinar:

September 9, 2026, at 10:30 a.m. Central Time

Please register at: https://attendee.gotowebinar.com/register/851469958176863836

Optional Facility Site Visit and Walk Through Logistical Information

HHSC will conduct one (1) optional site visit that will be held at the date and time described below. Attendance is optional.

September 11, 2026, at  10:00 a.m. Central Time

Pre-registration is requested to allow for space accommodation.

Please register for the site visit at: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/fkYtN1AkW6?origin=lprLink 


Refer to Section 2.1 (Project Location, Summary, and Budget) and Exhibit H – Site Visit Location of the RFP, for a physical address of Project location.

Description:  The City of San Antonio is soliciting proposals for a contractor to furnish all labor, equipment and materials necessary to install, maintain and remove City-owned LED holiday lighting on assorted trees and structures located in Downtown San Antonio. The services shall include, but are not limited to, the installation, maintenance, and removal of holiday lighting and running power cable(s) to permanent or temporary electrical panels.

 

ApplicableProduct Categories:

96246 –  Installation and Removal Services

28556 –  Lighting Fixtures, Outdoor: Floodlights,Spotlights, Yard Lights and All Other Weatherproof Fixtures, ExceptStreetlight, Including Recycled Types

 

Date Issued:  October 15, 2026

Due Date & Time:  November 16,2026, 11:00 a.m. Central Time

 

Pre-Submittal Conference:  Pre-Submittal Conference will be held at 9:00 a.m., Central Time, on October22, 2026, via Microsoft Teams. Attendance at thePre-Submittal Conference is optional, but highly encouraged. Respondents may call the toll-free number listed below and enter accesscode to participate the day of the conference.

 Dial-InNumber: 1-312-667-7136 | Phone Conference ID: 401 380 324#


Additionally, a sitevisit will be held at 1:00 p.m. Central Time on October 22, 2026. Please reference the RFCSP document for more information. 

To view this solicitation, go to the SAePS portal;  https://supplierservice.sanantonio.gov/irj/portal

If you have not completed theCity’s SAePS Vendor Registration, you must do so in order to view thesolicitation and submit a response. Once you have logged on to the SAePSportal, click on “My Bids” (first), if not viewable then click “Other Bids” (toview all already published competitive bids). Vendor Guides & Support can be accessed fromthis link:  https://www.sa.gov/Directory/Departments/Finance/About/Divisions/Procurement/Resources/Guides-Support

 

TO REGISTER:  You will need to complete the vendorregistration by accessing the SAePS Vendor Registration at https://www.sa.gov/Directory/Departments/Finance/About/Divisions/Procurement/Become-a-Vendor.   Questionsregarding registration may be submitted to Vendor Support at (210) 207-0118 orby email at vendors@sanantonio.gov with “SAePS Portal” on the subject line so this canbe expedited.

List.title: RFP 26-1392 EWCRWS Infrastructure and Expansion - Trinity Well and Phase 1D Project

Detail.title: RFP 26-1392 EWCRWS Infrastructure and Expansion - Trinity Well and Phase 1D Project
Detail.description:
The BRA is soliciting sealed proposals for the EWCRWS Infrastructure and Expansion


The “1B1D PROJECT” represents two critical expansion improvements to the Brazos River Authority’s (BRA) East Williamson County’s Regional Water System Water Treatment Plant (EWCWTP); Phase 1B and Phase 1D.

The Phase 1B Trinity Well Infrastructure Improvements will use cooling towers to treat up to 4 MGD of groundwater from the existing Trinity Well #1 for blending with treated surface water from Granger Lake. Trinity Well #1 is located on the campus of the EWCWTP.  Additionally, Phase 1B work located at the EWCWTP includes significant chemical monitoring and distribution systems, stormwater system, upgrades to electrical and automation, and access road improvements that provide future buildout resilience. Phase 1B has schedule priority.   

The Phase 1D Short-term Expansion continues improvements at the EWCWTP to treat up to 13 MGD of additional surface water from Granger Lake by expanding raw water pumping capacity, upgrading storage reservoir inlets, outlets, and pumping capacity, upgrades to existing chemical systems, upgrades to electrical and automation systems, new rapid mix system, two new clarifiers, modify piping at four existing filters, four new additional filter systems, new backwash basin demolition of existing components and structures being replaced or removed, an additional 4.25 MG of finished water storage capacity for storage of blended treated groundwater (from Phase 1B) with treated surface water (from Phase 1D), and access road improvements. Phase 1D also includes a new medium service pump station for transmission of the finished water to the BRA’s existing and potential new customers, while providing future buildout resilience for longer term expansion.

Detail.description: Bastrop County is requesting bids for a drainage improvement project on Cardinal Dr at the Alum Creek Tributary within the 100 Block of Cardinal Dr (Longitude 30.16495 Latitude -97.21293). This project area provides critical habitat for the federally endangered Houston Toad. Bastrop County will provide and deploy a permitted Houston Toad monitor for the duration of construction activities and all contracted personnel will be trained by a Houston Toad Biologist prior to commencing work. All avoidance and minimization measures are listed in the “Biological Resource Notes” in the General Notes page 2 of the plans and specifications. The submitted lump sum bids should be based on the installation of erosion control measures, determine and implementation of traffic control temporary access or detour, demolition of the two (2) existing 48” corrugated metal pipe culverts and roadway, grading, construction of two 8’ x 5’ Rigid Concrete Box culverts with headwalls and pavement repair, and stabilization of the project site.

Detail.description:
Mason County, Texas (the “County”) is soliciting Proposals from qualified and experienced consulting firms to prepare an update to the County’s Hazard Mitigation Plan (HMP) in accordance with the requirements set forth in this Solicitation (the submitting parties “Respondents” and the submissions “Proposals”). This project is funded through a grant administered by the Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM) and must comply with all requirements of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), including 44 CFR §201.6

The objective of this Solicitation is to identify and contract with a Respondent that demonstrates the capability, expertise, and resources necessary to deliver high-quality services that meet the operational and performance needs of THE COUNTY. The successful Respondent will be selected based on their demonstrated ability to satisfy the evaluation criteria described in this document.

All Proposals must be submitted in accordance with the instructions contained herein. Proposals that do not comply with the requirements and submission guidelines may be rejected as non-responsive.

List.title: Garth Road Reconstruction Phase 1
List.nigpCodes: 91327-Construction, Highway And Road;

Detail.title: Garth Road Reconstruction Phase 1
Detail.nigpCodes: 91327-Construction, Highway And Road;
Detail.description:
LEGAL NOTICE

Advertisement for Invitation for Bids


October 13, 2026


Notice is hereby given that sealed bids will be accepted by the Jefferson County Purchasing Department for Invitation for Bid (IFB 26-066/MR) Garth Road Reconstruction Phase 1.  Specifications for this project may be obtained from the Jefferson County website, https://jeffersoncountytx.gov/Purchasing/ or by calling 409-835-8593.


Bids are to be sealed and addressed to the Purchasing Agent with the bid number and name marked on the outside of the envelope or box.  Bidders shall forward an original and one (1) copy of their bid to the address shown below.  Jefferson County does not accept bids submitted electronically.  Late bids will be rejected as non-responsive. Bids will be publicly opened and read aloud in the Jefferson County Purchasing Department (1st  Floor, Historic Courthouse) 1149 Pearl Street, Beaumont, Texas 77701, at the time and date below.  Bidders are invited to attend the sealed bid opening.


BID NAME:        Garth Road Reconstruction Phase 1


BID NUMBER: IFB 26-066/MR


DUE BY TIME/DATE: 11:00 AM CT, Wednesday, November 4, 2026


MAIL OR DELIVER TO: Jefferson County Purchasing Department

1149 Pearl Street, 1st Floor

Beaumont, Texas  77701


There will be a Pre-Bid Conference and Walk-Through at 9:00 am CT on Thursday, October 22, 2026, at Jefferson County Engineering Department Conference Room located at 1149 Pearl Street, (Historic Courthouse 5th Floor), Beaumont, Texas 77701.  


The County shall require the Bidder to furnish a Bid Security in the amount of five percent (5%) of the total contract cost.  The bid bond must be executed with a surety company authorized to do business in the State of Texas.            


Within ten (10) days after the date of contract execution and prior to the issuance of Notice to Proceed and/or Purchase Order, the Bidder shall furnish the following bonds: Performance Bond to the County for the full amount of the contract if the contract exceeds fifty-thousand dollars ($50,000). Payment Bond to the County for the full amount of the contract if the contract exceeds twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000.00). 


Any questions relating to these bid requirements should be directed to Mistey Reeves, Assistant Purchasing Agent  at 409-835-8593 or via email at: mistey.reeves@jeffersoncountytx.gov.  If no response in 72 hours, contact Deborah Clark, Purchasing Agent at 409-835-8593 or via email at deb.clark@jeffersoncountytx.gov. 

 

Jefferson County encourages Disadvantaged Business Enterprises (DBE/ACDBEs), Minority/Women Business Enterprises (M/WBEs), Small Business Concerns (HUBZone) and Veteran Heroes United In Business (VetHUB) to participate in the bidding process. Jefferson County does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age or disability in employment, or the provisions of services. Individuals requiring special accommodations are requested to contact our office at least seven (7) days prior to the bid due date at 409-835-8593.


All interested firms are invited to submit a bid in accordance with the terms and conditions stated in this bid.


Bidders are strongly encouraged to carefully read the entire invitation, as failure to return and/or complete all required documentation will result in a response being declared as non-responsive.


                                                                                                                               

Deborah L. Clark, Purchasing Agent

Jefferson County, Texas

Detail.title: 26RFCSP85 Brushy Creek Trail Retaining Wall
Detail.description: Williamson County intends to implement improvements at the site to stabilize the existing retaining wall and address erosion and drainage concerns in the surrounding area. Williamson County owns and maintains the Brushy Creek Regional Trail which extends from Cedar Park east to the western edge of the City of Hutto. A portion of the trail located immediately downstream of the Upper Brushy Creek Water Control and Improvement District (UBCWCID) Dam No. 7 contains a retaining wall with pedestrian railing which runs along the northern edge of the trail approximately 170 feet. Recent inspection of the dam indicated cracking along the face of the existing retaining wall and localized erosion and washout observed at the base of the wall undercutting the structure.

Austin State Hospital

4110 Guadalupe St,Austin, TX 78751

Detail.title: Transportation Project Delivery Plan Consultant Services
Detail.nigpCodes: 91896-Transportation Consulting;
Detail.description:
H-GAC is seeking Statements of Qualifications from firms interested in developing a detailed, actionable plan to guide the development and long‑term success of a Transportation Project Delivery team responsible for delivering federally funded transportation projects.


To achieve this purpose, the Consultant will evaluate the MPO’s existing project delivery framework by assessing current capabilities, organizational structure, team roles, and operational gaps; define the appropriate scope of delivery involvement through stakeholder engagement and peer analysis; and develop recommendations for structuring, resourcing, and integrating the team into MPO operations. This effort will also establish standardized budgets for project delivery services; define processes for project selection, initiation, and procurement for the delivery program; and develop consistent procedures to execute and close out (pre-construction) projects in compliance with all applicable Federal and State requirements.

List.title: NASPO ValuePoint RFP NVP_1443 Idaho Medical Supplies

Detail.title: NASPO ValuePoint RFP NVP_1443 Idaho Medical Supplies
Detail.description:
The NASPO ValuePoint Request for Proposal (RFP) for Medical Supplies was released by the State of Idaho on September 25, 2026. The RFP number is 1433. All vendor proposals must be submitted by 6:00 p.m., Central Time (5:00 p.m., Mountain Time) on November 9, 2026.

The purpose of this Request for Proposal (RFP) is to establish Master Agreements with qualified bidders. The objective of this RFP is to obtain best value, and in some cases achieve more favorable pricing, than is obtainable by an individual state or local government entity because of the collective volume of potential purchases by numerous state and local government entities.

The Master Agreement(s) resulting from this procurement may be used by state governments (including departments, agencies,institutions), institutions of higher education, political subdivisions (i.e.,colleges, school districts, counties, cities, etc.), the District of Columbia, territories of the United States, and other eligible entities subject to approval of the individual chief procurement official and compliance with localstatutory and regulatory provisions.

 

The RFP is available on Idaho's procurement system website using the following link: https://sms-idaho-prd.tam.inforgov.com/fsm/SupplyManagementSupplier/form/SourcingEvent%5BByCompany%5D%28200,1433%29.XiSupplierPortalSummary?action=_open&list=SourcingEvent%5BByCompany%5D%28_niu_,_niu_%29.HomeEvents&csk.SupplierGroup=LUMA&sortOrderName=SourcingEvent.ByCompany&previousDisabled=true&fk=SourcingEvent%5BByCompany%5D%28198,1368%29&firstDisabled=true&hasPrevious=false&pageSize=10&hasNext=true&isAscending=true&lk=SourcingEvent%5BByCompany%5D%28285,1439%29&pk=SourcingEvent%5BByCompany%5D&selectedPanel=Attachments or the ValuePoint website at: https://www.naspovaluepoint.org/solicitations/.

 

Important Dates:

Dates and deadlines are subject to change. Offerors should continue checking the RFP Website for the most up-to-date information.

List.title: 3202600156 Open Enrollment (OE) for Diabetes Self-Management Education Services

Detail.title: 3202600156 Open Enrollment (OE) for Diabetes Self-Management Education Services
Detail.description: TWC’s mission is to promote and support a workforce system that creates value and offers employers, families, individuals and communities the opportunity to achieve and sustain economic prosperity.This Open Enrollment is for Diabetes Self-Management Education Services. Diabetes self-management education is the process of developing the customer's knowledge, skills, and abilities that are necessary to manage diabetes and improve his or her health outcomes. Vocational Rehabilitation (VR) customers might require education about diabetes to address the cause of the disease. Diabetes self-management education provides adaptive techniques and/or equipment to help the customer self-manage his or her diabetes.Assessment and teaching of blood sugar monitoring, medication delivery, and other self-care skills related to diabetes self-management require close, hands-on evaluation and training when working with individuals who are blind or visually impaired.Diabetes self-management education services are based on the Association of Diabetes Care and Education Specialist’s 7 Self-Care Behaviors, which are:• healthy eating;• being active;• monitoring;• taking medications;• healthy coping;• problem solving; and• reducing risk.Diabetes self-management education services are for customers who:• are newly diagnosed;• need surgery or a medical procedure and are at risk of further complications because of poor diabetes management;• are unable to maintain employment because of their diabetes;• need additional training about diabetes management after losing their sight;• must self-manage diabetes for admittance to training programs and for full participation in training such as that offered by the Criss Cole Rehabilitation Center;• cannot benefit from community-based educational programs; and/or• have unique needs that cannot be met through medical providers paid through the Maximum Affordable Payment Schedule.

Detail.description: The Texas Racing Commission (TXRC) is publishing this Request for Proposal (RFP) for Stewards in Training to perform Services (Class 958/81) within the State of Texas. TXRC intends to make an award of at least one (1) or more contracts. Individual Blanket contract will not exceed $75,000.00 per fiscal year.
Detail.addendum: 9/24/2026 2:19 pm: ADDENDUM – STEWARDS IN TRAINING STAFFING REQUIREMENTS Our agency specializes in the horse racing industry, and due to the specialized nature of this work and the very low volume of qualified applicants, it is necessary to keep the solicitation open. Maintaining access to qualified veterinary professionals is critical to the agency’s ability to fulfill its statutory and operational responsibilities. Texas Racing Commission (TXRC) hires contractors to serve as Stewards-in-Training. They shadow seasoned officials to learn how to enforce the Texas Racing Act and the TXRC Rules of Racing at licensed horse racetracks. Scope of Responsibilities: Operational guidelines, Stewards in Training perform complex legal and technical officiating work under the direct supervision of the Chief Steward. They serve as temporary, journey-level regulatory contractors across licensed Texas horse racetracks. Given these statutory and regulatory requirements, maintaining an active solicitation is necessary to ensure the agency has continued access to qualified and specialized professionals. Closing the solicitation due to the limited applicant pool could create a significant staffing risk and potentially impact the agency’s ability to meet its regulatory obligations and maintain uninterrupted operations. Accordingly, we recommend that the solicitation remain open to allow the agency to continue identifying and recruiting qualified candidates as they become available.

Detail.title: Capital Planning Software Solution
Detail.nigpCodes:
20800-Computer Software For Microcomputers, Systems, Including Cloud;
20900-Computer Software For Mini And Mainframe Computers (Preprogrammed);
Detail.description:
1) Intent of RFI: The Texas Facilities Commission is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to solicit information regarding commercially available capital planning software solutions capable of meeting the needs of TFC's Planning and Design Division. 


a) This document is intended to solicit responses from individuals, firms, teams, or organizations that develop, sell, or implement capital planning software. Respondents with experience serving public entities and large, multi-building facility portfolios are particularly encouraged to respond.

   

2) Inquiry Only: This is an inquiry only. No contract or agreement will be entered into as a result of this process, nor does a response to this document initiate a formal procurement or represent a commitment to issue a Request for Qualifications (“RFQ”) or Request for Proposals (“RFP”) in the future. Those choosing to respond to this RFI will not, merely by virtue of submitting such a response, be deemed to be “bidders” on the Project in any sense, and no such Respondent will have any preference, special designation, advantage or disadvantage whatsoever in any subsequent activities related to the Project. The information contained in the responses to this RFI will help the TFC to advance scope development, budgetary estimates and legislative appropriation request, which may result in the launch of a formal solicitation and associated procurement activities. Responding to this RFI will not prohibit, debar, or disqualify any future solicitation opportunities.


SECTION II - BACKGROUND


1) General:


a) The Texas Facilities Commission manages over fourteen (14) million square feet of state-owned properties including office spaces, storage areas, warehouses, schools, medical labs, parking lots, and garages throughout the state. TFC does this with a combination of in-house and contracted staff for the various specialties and trades needed to build, support and maintain these properties.


b) TFC's Planning and Design Division is responsible for long-range facility planning, conducting facility condition assessments, prioritizing the State's deferred maintenance backlog, and developing capital budgets in support of legislative appropriations requests.


c) Any resulting software capability is intended to serve as a decision-support tool for TFC within their current statutory role and is not intended to establish new regulatory authority, policy-making functions, or ongoing service obligations beyond those already assigned to and resourced by  TFC.


2) Purpose:


a) The purpose of this RFI is to solicit information from certified software vendors, resellers, and implementers on:


i) Capabilities of commercially available capital planning software.

ii) Typical licensing, pricing, and implementation models for such software.

iii) Typical support model, staffing and budgetary needs to maintain the solution.

iv) Recommendations on how the State of Texas should approach implementation to ensure complete functionality.

v) Common challenges to avoid when selecting and implementing this type of software.

vi) Capabilities to support space inventory management, space allocation and assignment tracking by occupying agency, and space utilization/consolidation planning integrated with facility condition and capital planning data.


SCHEDULE OF EVENTS: TFC reserves the right to change the dates shown below.

EVENT - DATE

Issue RFI - 9/23/2026

Deadline for Submission of Questions - 10/15/2026

Deadline for Submission of Responses - 11/30/2026 - Monday, 3:00 PM

List.title: Ready Workforce Training Pipeline

Detail.title: Ready Workforce Training Pipeline
Detail.description:
This solicitation is being reissued and will remain open indefinitely. Interested vendors may submit a response at any time. Responses will be accepted and reviewed on a rolling basis until further notice.

Workforce Solutions Borderplex (WSB) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to gather comprehensive data regarding existing workforce education, training, and apprenticeship programs that prepare individuals for careers supporting data centers and related infrastructure projects. This RFI is for information gathering and strategic planning purposes only and does not constitute a formal procurement or solicitation for services.

Objective:
The Borderplex region is seeing rapid growth in AI infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, energy, utilities, and telecommunications. The goal of this RFI is to:

  • Identify existing regional resources and training capabilities.

  • Understand the current workforce training landscape.

  • Identify programs that can support future demand for skilled occupations in the construction and long-term operation of data centers.

Target Respondents:
WSB invites responses from education providers, training organizations, registered apprenticeship programs, labor organizations, employers, industry associations, and other workforce development partners.

Background:
As national initiatives emerge to accelerate workforce preparation through employer-connected training models, WSB is interested in understanding the current resources available to meet anticipated industry growth. Information gathered will be used to increase awareness of training opportunities that support regional job seekers and the economy.

Detail.description: This Open Enrollment is for Project Search. Project SEARCH is an international initiative that supports partnerships among businesses (employers), local school districts, vocational rehabilitation (VR) agencies, and other entities that serve individuals with disabilities, including intellectual and developmental disabilities. Project SEARCH promotes the successful long-term employment of VR customers in jobs that are stable, meaningful, integrated, and competitively compensated. Project SEARCH prepares students with disabilities for the workforce through total immersion in a business environment where students develop competitive, marketable, and transferable skills. The program is conducted for a full academic year. Each VR customer completes Asset Discovery, has the opportunity to build skills through three (3) unpaid internship rotations, and receives assistance in securing permanent, long-term, competitive employment.

Detail.description: The Texas Racing Commission (TXRC) is publishing this Request for Qualifications (RFQ) for Veterinarian Physicians to perform Veterinarian Medical Services (Class 961-86) within the State of Texas. TXRC intends to make an award to at least one (1) or more qualified vendors. Individual Blanket Contracts will not exceed $150,000.00 per fiscal year.
Detail.addendum:
8/24/2026 1:21 pm: ADDENDUM – VETERINARY STAFFING REQUIREMENTS Our agency specializes in the horse racing industry, and due to the specialized nature of this work and the very low volume of qualified applicants, it is necessary to keep the solicitation open. Maintaining access to qualified veterinary professionals is critical to the agency’s ability to fulfill its statutory and operational responsibilities. Texas law requires veterinarians and, by extension, licensed veterinary technicians to be employed and appropriately supervised at racetracks operating under the jurisdiction of the Texas Racing Commission. Statutory Requirement Under Texas Occupations Code § 2023.103, each race meeting conducted under the Commission’s jurisdiction must have at least one state veterinarian. Administrative Requirements: "The Texas Rules of Racing (Part 8 of Title 16 of the Texas Administrative Code) establish" Horse Racetracks: At least two veterinarians are required, including Commission veterinarians. Veterinary Technicians: Licensed veterinary technicians may be required to support veterinary operations and must work under the appropriate veterinary supervision. Supervision: Commission veterinarians oversee veterinary personnel and veterinary technicians at the racetrack. Scope of Responsibilities: Veterinary personnel support critical regulatory and operational functions, including pre-race examinations, drug testing, stable inspections, injury documentation, and emergency veterinary care. Given these statutory and regulatory requirements, maintaining an active solicitation is necessary to ensure the agency has continued access to qualified and specialized veterinary professionals. Closing the solicitation due to the limited applicant pool could create a significant staffing risk and potentially impact the agency’s ability to meet its regulatory obligations and maintain uninterrupted operations. Accordingly, we recommend that the solicitation remain open to allow the agency to continue identifying and recruiting qualified candidates as they become available.

Detail.nigpCodes:
91450-Heating, Ventilating And Air Conditioning (Hvac);

Detail.description:
INTERESTED VENDORS NEED TO REGISTER AND VIEW THIS BID OPPORTUNITY AT: HTTPS://ALIEFISD.IONWAVE.NET.

Alief Independent School District is seeking catalog discount pricing for HVAC-Miscellaneous Repair Parts and Supplies. This proposal applies to but is not limited to, the following categories: HVAC Miscellaneous Repair Parts and Supplies. Awards will be made to multiple vendors incrementally during the solicitation offering period. However, VENDORS SHOULD RESPOND ASAP. Initial awards will be made at the August 2023 school board meeting. The contract term shall be for four (4) years beginning September 1, 2023, and ending August 31, 2027. Proposal responses will be accepted continually until 2:00 P.M. CDT on August 31, 2027. Vendors may cancel during the contract term by notifying the Buyer of record. Responses should be submitted electronically; award notices will be sent electronically. No faxed, late, or e-mailed responses will be accepted. Requests for additional information or clarification on information contained in this RFP must be submitted via the Questions Tab within the electronic bid opportunity by noon CDT on 08/15/2027. Response to questions will be posted in the Questions Tab periodically. Alief ISD reserves the right to waive all formalities, be the sole judge of quality and suitability, and reject any or all proposals.

List.title: Operational Support Contracted Services

Detail.title: Operational Support Contracted Services
Detail.description:
Leander Independent School District (known herein as "LISD" or "District") is accepting proposal responses from vendors interested in providing the following products or services:

Operational Support Contracted Services

Leander ISD is accepting proposals from vendors to provide operational support contracted services in accordance with the instructions, terms and conditions and requirements/specifications contained in this solicitation. This solicitation is issued per Texas Education Code Chapter 44, Sub Chapter B.

NOTE: The services included in this solicitation do not include construction-related services that qualify under Texas Government Code 2269.

NOTE TO INTERESTED VENDORS: Leander ISD seeks to create a list of awarded Contractors to provide a varied list of services. Examples of contracted services the District is requesting proposals for are, but are not limited to:

Access Control Services

Arbor Tree Services

Custodial Equipment Maintenance and Repair Equipment Rentals

Glass Services

Industrial Equipment Maintenance and Repair

Landscape Services

Locksmith Services

Maintenance Equipment Maintenance and Repair

Material Handling Equipment Maintenance and Repair

Overhead Door Maintenance and Repair

Parking Lot Maintenance Towing Services

Transportation Ride Share Services

Other services identified to be operational support that are not listed above

When LISD has a need for these services, LISD may use the list of vendors as a primary source to obtain the services. There is no obligation upon LISD to use any particular Contractor and there is no guarantee of any quantity of orders. LISD will choose the Contractor that best meets its needs. 

Vendors are able to view more about this opportunity by visiting https://leanderisd.ionwave.net/CurrentSourcingEvents.aspx.
